assumptions: Definition 1 prompt process and Definition 2 uniform-attention predictor.
Assumption 1 bounded task functions and Assumption 2 bounded i.i.d. inputs with conditional independence.
Compact prompt component supports with finite diameters.
The Bayes predictor is alpha-Hölder with alpha in (0,1] and constant L.
The encoder and decoder have the stated Lipschitz constants and model output is bounded by B_M.
Only the input distribution shifts; task and noise distributions are unchanged.
domain: Every parameter theta and every pair of source/target prompt laws satisfying the assumptions.
quantifiers: The bound holds separately at every k=1,...,p and is averaged over k.
interpretation_boundary: The theorem does not assert R_PV^(P)=R_PV^(Q). Intrinsic to the target domain means model-independent after the target law is fixed.
acceptance: Derive the exact architectural Holder modulus Lambda_alpha.
Prove the expectation bound directly for every coupling and take the Wasserstein infimum.
Use exact rational checkers for component inequalities.
Reject an incorrect posterior-variance invariance interpretation with an assumption-satisfying counterexample.
Inherit and rerun all accepted claim checks.
non_circularity: No Wasserstein radius or tolerance is selected. The argument is a universal coupling inequality; finite exact sweeps are independent bug detectors.
